branches.reason: Cross-referencing the nine supplied NL contracts against the exact source inventory and closed FCSTM inventory shows all endpoint, containment, and initial-entry obligations are satisfied by exact matching edges/states. The root initial edge [*]->InitialState (transition:line:12) is owned by the root composite state:llms_emp_feedback_final_0011, and InitialState has the exact outgoing edge to BrakingState (transition:line:13), jointly realizing NL2-INITENTRY-1's operating entry-point obligation. NL2-ENDPOINT-1 (InitialState->OperationalState) matches transition:line:14 exactly. NL2-ENDPOINT-2 (BrakingState->InitialState) matches transition:line:17 exactly. NL3-ENDPOINT-1 (BrakingState->ClampingState) matches transition:line:15 exactly. The DERIVED-b0db3a5e contract (OperationalState->InitialState) matches transition:line:16 exactly. All four containment contracts (NL2-CONTAINMENT-1, NL2-CONTAINMENT-2, NL3-CONTAINMENT-1, DERIVED-0d781e3b7de7736f4635) are satisfied because InitialState, BrakingState, OperationalState, and ClampingState are all direct children of the single root composite per closed_model_inventory parent fields, matching the informally-scoped 'basic braking device' root scope stated in NL. No transition-group guard collision exists: ALT-NL2-BRAKING (triggered by an event) and ALT-NL2-OPERATIONAL (guarded by a distinct failure condition) are not operationally indistinguishable under the same condition, since one is event-driven and the other is guard-driven on a different signal outcome, so guard_disjointness does not apply. No wrong local-exit target is found: both return transitions (BrakingState->InitialState, OperationalState->InitialState) resolve to the exact named InitialState. No supplied contract has property=cardinality, so no cardinality_bindings rows are required. Since every supplied and branch-local derived contract's exact locus, endpoint, and containment identity closes without a structural/contrastive defect, this lens emits no candidates, no additional_contracts, and no unresolved rows; the full contract set is preserved by omission per the sparse-response protocol.

branches.reason: This lens audits root reachability, event-consumer coverage, dead-end/frontier facts, and termination continuation for the basic braking device model. The closed FCSTM shows all six states reachable from root, all five declared events have a reachable consumer, and the two leaf states (ClampingState, ClampingLoseState) are reachable dead ends with no outgoing transition. Since no supplied NL contract establishes ClampingState or ClampingLoseState as an operating scope requiring continued progress, deadlock_freedom is not independently obligated by any atomic contract; the leaf facts are recorded only as supporting context. The initial_entry contract (owner=root/basic braking device, target=BrakingState) is satisfied by tr_0002/transition:line:13 which fires on Brake_Signal_Received, so it is omitted. The endpoint contracts for initial->operational (signal transmission fails), braking->initial (signal feedback sent), operational->initial (signal feedback sent, derived), and braking->clamping (entering clamping state) are all satisfied by exact existing transitions with matching triggers, so they are omitted as non-issues under this lens. Containment contracts are satisfied because all named states are direct children of the single flat root scope. No cardinality contracts are supplied. The only behaviorally consequential candidate this lens surfaces is a derived reachable dead-end obligation: NL3 establishes that after entering BrakingState the system must reach ClampingState, and the closed model shows ClampingState is a reachable leaf with zero outgoing transitions and no declared termination semantics, meaning the device permanently halts there with no way to resume braking-device operation (no return path to InitialState/OperationalState cycle). This is a distinct dead_end property from the already-satisfied transition_endpoints contract and is preserved as a predicate-null W1 candidate because V1(initial_scope) is registered for deadlock-frontier facts, but this dead-end is not accompanied by an explicit progress/response obligation on ClampingState from NL, so I use the LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING deterministic fact only as supporting evidence for a predicate-null observation rather than fabricating a progress contract absent from NL. I therefore keep this as a single derived candidate, distinct from the satisfied NL3 endpoint contract, rather than omitting the dead-end fact entirely, since the NL text ('final execution unit for train braking operations') combined with the reachable-leaf/no-continuation fact represents a precise structural gap worth preserving for downstream W1 adjudication.

stage_receipts.reason: Three numbered NL segments were analyzed. NL1 is purely descriptive context about the device's role and is marked context with no contract since it establishes no obligation. NL2 establishes: (a) initial_entry into the braking state upon receiving a brake signal (treated as the first operating transition from the initial state), (b) an alternative endpoint from braking-state-triggering condition to the operational state when signal transmission fails, (c) a return endpoint from the operating flow back to the initial state upon signal feedback sent. These are captured as a transition group sharing source (the state entered on brake signal, i.e., the braking-flow source) with alternatives, plus discrete transition_endpoints contracts for each exact edge, since alternative destinations must be separate endpoint contracts per instructions. NL3 continues the narrative: after entering the braking state, transitions to the brake caliper clamping state, extracted as one endpoint contract sourced from the braking state. All segments are marked covered since each carries at least one atomic contract with its own segment_id.
